topic: A Legally Grounded Empirical Evaluation of Explainable AI for Consumer Credit Scoring
note: Semantic Scholar bulk-search syntax: "phrase", + (AND), | (OR), * (prefix). Discovery only, not evidence.
queries: ("credit scoring" | "credit risk" | lending | loan*) + (explainab* | interpretab* | XAI)
("explanation quality" | "evaluating explanations" | "XAI evaluation" | faithfulness | "explanation stability") + (explainab* | XAI | attribution*)
broad_queries: ("explanation quality" | "evaluating explanations" | "XAI evaluation" | faithfulness | "explanation stability") + (explainab* | XAI | attribution*)
screening_note: Papers hit only by broad_queries are screened by a local model; papers hit by any other query are kept without LLM screening (eval: corpus_silver_v1).
screening_topic: Literature screening for a thesis on explainable credit scoring. The paper is RELEVANT if it matches ANY ONE of these facets (it does NOT need to match several): (a) machine-learning or statistical models for credit scoring, credit risk or loan default, even without explainability; (b) explainability or interpretability methods applied to credit, lending or financial decisions; (c) evaluating explanation quality (faithfulness, stability, fairness of explanations) of SHAP, LIME or counterfactual explainers; (d) legal or regulatory transparency/explanation requirements for automated credit decisions or profiling; (e) fairness or discrimination in credit or lending. Use UNCERTAIN when a paper is peripheral to these facets, e.g. general finance AI surveys.
